H1.claim: Allied expenditure outcomes differ across pathways by more than the reserve channel does
H1.headline: median scored separation 0.74 sd, 2.2 times the reserve channel (0.34 sd); largest NATO Europe at 1.18 sd, smallest Indo-Pacific allies at 0.32 sd; descriptive, not a significance test

H2.claim: Allied expenditure responds more strongly to US expenditure than to Chinese expenditure
H2.verdict: not supported at the 5 percent level
H2.headline: pooled panel of 45 countries, 1991 to 2025: b_us 0.16 (se 0.091), b_cn -0.056 (se 0.075), difference in magnitudes 0.105, one-sided p 0.12; 2025: United States -7.5 percent, NATO Europe +15.6 percent

H3.claim: Reserve composition responds least to the pathway, and the dollar's decline does not accrue to the renminbi
H3.headline: expenditure coefficient +0.93 pp, 95 percent interval -0.94 to 2.80; dollar share separation 0.34 sd; renminbi 3.1 percent of payments against 2.11 percent of reserves (2026-06, gap 0.99 pp); other commercial channels not simulated
